title.en: The Middle Ages & the Islamic Golden Age
title.zh: 中世纪与伊斯兰黄金时代

clips.send: Rome. Home of the pope, head of the Catholic Church in western Europe.
clips.text: Rome. Home of the pope, head of the Catholic Church in western Europe.

clips.send: Myth: “The Dark Ages” — historians avoid the term today: the period gave us universities, cathedrals, Magna Carta and the House of Wisdom.
clips.text: Myth: “The Dark Ages” — historians avoid the term today: the period gave us universities, cathedrals, Magna Carta and the House of Wisdom.

clips.send: Damascus. Capital of the Umayyad caliphs (661–750).
clips.text: Damascus. Capital of the Umayyad caliphs (661–750).

clips.send: Paris. Capital of the French kings; its university grew around 1200; Notre-Dame was begun in 1163.
clips.text: Paris. Capital of the French kings; its university grew around 1200; Notre-Dame was begun in 1163.

clips.send: Historians call 476–1500 in Europe the Middle Ages (中世纪) — the “middle” between ancient Rome and the modern world. Memory hook“476 the West falls, 800 Charlemagne crowned, 843 split in three, 1453 the East falls.”
clips.text: Historians call 476–1500 in Europe the Middle Ages (中世纪) — the “middle” between ancient Rome and the modern world. 🎵 Memory hook“476 the West falls, 800 Charlemagne crowned, 843 split in three, 1453 the East falls.”

clips.send: Jerusalem. A holy city for Jews, Christians and Muslims — the goal of the Crusades.
clips.text: Jerusalem. A holy city for Jews, Christians and Muslims — the goal of the Crusades.

clips.send: Constantinople (Istanbul). Byzantine capital, guarded by huge triple land walls; on the trade route between Europe and Asia.
clips.text: Constantinople (Istanbul). Byzantine capital, guarded by huge triple land walls; on the trade route between Europe and Asia.

clips.send: Frankish kingdom. Clovis united the Franks and founded the kingdom (486); he became a Christian, winning the support of the Church. Most of today’s France and western Germany.
clips.text: Frankish kingdom. Clovis united the Franks and founded the kingdom (486); he became a Christian, winning the support of the Church.. Most of today’s France and western Germany.

clips.send: Eastern Roman Empire. When the West fell in 476, the East — rich, with strong walls around Constantinople — survived. Greek-speaking, Christian, and still calling itself “Roman”.
clips.text: Eastern Roman Empire. When the West fell in 476, the East — rich, with strong walls around Constantinople — survived.. Greek-speaking, Christian, and still calling itself “Roman”.

clips.send: Samarkand. A Silk Road city; paper-making was known here by the 700s.
